3.      PUBLIC HEARING


        a)   BYLAW NO. 1883
             "Langford Zoning Bylaw, Amendment No. 581, (2627 Sooke Rd), Bylaw No. 1883, 2020".

The Mayor opened the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1893 at 5:34 pm, and read a statement to inform those
present of the public hearing procedure.

Director of Planning Matthew Baldwin advised that Danny Jadresko, has applied on behalf of Woodsmere
Holdings Corp to amend the zoning of 2627 Sooke Roadfrom the R2 (One- and Two-Family Residential) Zone
to the C9 (Community Town Centre Pedestrian 9) Zone.

This is being proposed in order to allow for the development of approximately 90-units and a single ground
level commercial unit that faces Sooke Road.

                                                                                                                June 29, 2020
                                                                                                                  Page 2 of 12


As part of this application, a public hearing is required in accordance with the regulations of the Local
Government Act.


In support of this application, the applicant has agreed to provide the following:

a) That the applicant provides, as a bonus for increased density, the following contributions per residential
          unit, prior to issuance of a building permit:

           i.     $610 towards the Affordable Housing Fund; and
          ii.     $2,074 toward the General Amenity Fund.

subject to reductions depending on the use and height in accordance with the Affordable Housing and
Amenity Contribution Policy.

b) That the applicant provides, prior to Public Hearing, the following:

           i.     A technical memo from an engineer that verifies storm water can be adequately managed on-site
                  for the proposed developments, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering.

c)        That the applicant provides, prior to Bylaw Adoption, a section 219 covenant, registered in priority of
          all other charges on title, that agrees to the following;

           i.     That all frontage improvements along Sooke Road are provided as per the Sooke Road Corridor
                  Concept Plan, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering and the Ministry of Transportation
                  and Infrastructure, and that any road dedication required to contain these frontage
                  improvements within the road right of way is provided prior to the issuance of a Building Permit;
          ii.     That a storm water management plan be provided prior to issuance of a building permit and
                  implemented, as per Bylaw 1000, all to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;
      iii.        That a construction parking and traffic management plan be provide prior to the issuance of a
                  building permit, to the satisfaction of the Director of Engineering;
      iv.         That an SRW for emergency access through the site is registered on title prior to the issuance of
                  a Building Permit;
          v.      That a separate covenant be registered prior to issuance of a building permit for the proposed
                  residential building that ensures parking is assigned and tied to each unit created in accordance
                  with the minimum required parking stalls as per the zoning bylaw.

d)             Authorize the Director of Planning to issue the following variance in the Form and Character
               Development Permit for 2627 Sooke Road:

     i.         That Table 1 of Section 4.01.01 be varied to reduce the minimum parking requirement from the
                required 2.75 spaces per dwelling unit with two bedrooms or less and 3.75 spaces per dwelling unit
                with more than two bedrooms to 1.25 spaces per dwelling unit with two bedrooms or less and 2.75
                spaces per dwelling unit with more than two bedrooms.

This proposal is consistent with the Official Community Plan Neighborhood Centre designation.

Notifications and advertisements have been placed as required by the Local Government Act.

                                                                                                           June 29, 2020
                                                                                                             Page 3 of 12


The Mayor called a first time for presentations.

Neighbourhood resident - This building will cause up to 180 extra vehicles plus visitor vehicles to enter a
quiet neighbourhood every day, causing increased traffic, parking concerns, and safety concerns. It will
decrease property values and impact current residents' enjoyment of their property. Resident requested
more information about any traffic studies done for this application. Neighbourhood streets are poorly
maintained and this will cause them to get worse. In the past, inadequate snow clearing has caused
HandyDART and BC Ambulance to refuse to come.

Resident on Ernhill Drive - The resident bought their property because the community is quiet. They have
complained about development in part, and think further development unacceptable. They think current
residents are being driven away, and that no improvements such as lights or speed bumps have been made
by the city. They believe traffic should not be directed through a quiet neighborhood, but should go through
the highway instead.

Neighbourhood resident-The resident asked why traffic needs to be routed through a quiet neighborhood
where children frequently play. There is currently little infrastructure, and no sidewalks or lights. The
resident said there are currently 58 residents, and that this proposal will double traffic in the neighborhood.
In addition, it is already difficult to drive in when it snows, and the proposal will reduce parking and force
visitors to park on the street. The resident thinks this will negatively affect property values. They said this is
not in line with OCP, and that this is not best suited to the surrounding properties.

Resident on Southglen Drive - The resident asked if the road will be widened. They believe it is not large
enough for this proposal, especially when it snows

Resident on Southglen Drive - The resident has lived here for a number of years, and thinks there is a nice
mix of ages between adults, seniors, and children. They think increased traffic will double the vehicles
parking in the area, and that the streets are already too congested. They are strongly opposed to this
proposal, and think access to the site should be from elsewhere.

Neighbourhood resident - The resident likes how quiet the neighborhood is, they had previously lived in a
very congested neighborhood before moving here. They think this proposal will cause the same issue, and
fear the impact of construction on residents' daily lives will change how kids can play on the street.

Mayor Young called a second time for presentations.

Resident on Ernhill Drive - The resident thinks the neighborhood has well-established and maintained
homes, and that this is not a neighborhood in transition. The resident referred to the report of a similar
development in the Sooke Road corridor, but stated there are no other developments that will impact quiet
streets like this. They stated that Happy Valley to Jacklin Road is the busiest corridor in Langford, and that
they cannot add more traffic to it as the parking requirements are inadequate.

Councillor Blackwell - Asked if the traffic can go on a different route or reduce its density.

M. Mahovlich, Director of Engineering - Stated that the Ministry of Transportation and Infrastructure did

                                                                                                        June 29, 2020
                                                                                                          Page 4 of 12


not prefer traffic to go along Sooke Road.

Councillor Sahlstrom - Asked what prevents us from having a left-hand turn into the development instead
of going through quiet streets?

Councillor Stewart - Suggested making the building for seniors only.

Mayor Young - Suggested the city work with the Ministry of Transportation and Infrastructure to develop a
Sooke Road access option as an alternative.

M. Mahovlich, Director of Engineering - Stated she can discuss a new plan with highways, but that it may
be contrary to the corridor masterplan.

Mayor Young called a third and final time for speakers.

Stephen Earnest with Woodsmere Holdings, Developer - The Developer stated that peak hours would have
24 vehicles in the afternoon, and that traffic leaves onto Sooke Road going right.

Neighbourhood resident - The resident thought the neighborhood cannot accommodate the incoming
construction traffic.


Councillor Seaton - Expressed his concerns about routes and overall parking reduction from this proposal.

M. Baldwin, Director of Planning - Stated that parking would be the same as the downtown core, and that
only residential traffic would go through the residential streets.

Councillor Szpak - Stated that she echoes the concerns about traffic flow.


Mayor Young then declared the Public Hearing for Bylaw No. 1893 closed at 6:13 p.m.

     a) That Section 6.41.06(l)(a) of Zoning Bylaw No. 300 be varied to reduce the setback between a
        building and a front or exterior side lot line from 7.5m to Om;

        building and a rear lot line from 3m to Om; and
